title: Droplet microfluidic-based loop-mediated isothermal amplification (dLAMP) for simultaneous quantification of multiple targets
protocol: Fabricate microfluidic chips.
Use AutoCAD or similar software to draw the Y-shape droplet microfluidic chip and droplet counting microwell chip pattern.
Order the photolithography mask with the designed pattern from a commercial supplier.
Fabricate microfluidic chips following established protocols.
Remove bubbles when bonding the chip.
Infiltrate Y-shape droplet microfluidic chip and droplet counting microwell chip channel with 0.1% (v/v) perfluorododecyltrichlorosilane (FTCS) solution in dry toluene for 5 min.
Wear appropriate protective clothing when handling FTCS solution.
Flush the microfluidic channels with pure HFE-7500 fluorinated oil to remove unreacted silanes.
Flush each module with pressurized air or nitrogen.
Store chips at 20°C–25°C before use, avoiding direct sunlight and dust contamination.
Heat HCV and HIV plasmids to 95°C for 5 minutes.
Cool the heated HCV and HIV plasmids in an ice/water mixture for at least 20 minutes before use.
Prepare the master mix for LAMP reaction in a microcentrifuge tube.
Add 1 μL of HCV plasmid, 1 μL of HIV plasmid, and 23 μL of LAMP master mix to a respective PCR 8-Tube strip.
Gently mix by pipetting 7-10 times.
Spin PCR 8-Tube Strip tubes lightly in a Benchtop centrifuge at 2,000 × g for roughly 10 seconds.
Run the LAMP reaction at 64°C using a C1000 Thermal Cycler with a CFX96 detection system.
Monitor real-time fluorescence intensity in ROX and Cy5 channels at intervals of 30 seconds for 100 cycles.
Heat the reaction products to 80°C for 20 minutes to stop the LAMP reaction by denaturing the polymerase.
Clean the microfluidic chips with Kimwipes and ethanol to remove dust and particles.
Prepare two sterile 1-mL syringes to inject continuous phase consisting of fluorinated oil Novec-7500 containing 1% (wt/wt) Pico-SurfTM fluorinated surfactant.
Filtrate the prepared oil phase with polyethersulfone membranes or cellulose acetate membranes with a pore size of 0.1/0.2 μm.
Prepare the multiplexed dLAMP reaction master mix A in a microcentrifuge tube.
Store master mix A at 4°C for up to 1 week.
Prepare the multiplexed dLAMP reaction master mix B in another microcentrifuge tube.
Optionally, add BSA (0.2 mg/mL) to master mix B to stabilize the enzyme and reduce loss during pipetting.
Use two 1-mL disposable sterile syringes (26 gauge) to inject dLAMP reaction master mix A.
Use a second syringe to inject dLAMP reaction master mix B.
Connect the syringes to the corresponding entrances of the Y-shape droplet microfluidic chip through PTFE microtubes and PEEK adapters.
Set injection flow rates to 10 μL/min for oil phases and 3 μL/min for aqueous phases during droplet generation.
Connect the droplet generation chip exit to the droplet counting microwell chip with a PTFE microtube and PEEK adapters to collect generated droplets.
Observe the flow junction of the droplet generation chip under a microscope with a 10 × objective.
Purge air from the chip with buffer solution, wait until droplet generation stabilizes, then collect droplets.
Observe the collection chip to monitor the droplet generation process.
Ensure that droplets are round with uniform diameters (∼50 μm).
Verify that droplets are monodispersed in the chamber.
Detach the full droplet counting microwell chip from the droplet generation chip when ready.
Connect a new droplet counting microwell chip to the exit of the droplet generation chip for another sample.
Use a new injector when injecting a different sample and discard the first two minutes' droplets.
Place the droplet counting microwell chips in a thermostat water bath (64°C) after collecting the droplets.
Seal the droplet counting microwell chips with tape to prevent loss of droplets during incubation.
Optimize the dLAMP reaction time to allow the stabilization of fluorescent droplet generation.
Incubate the samples for 60 minutes as per the optimized reaction time.
Remove the droplet counting microwell chips from the LAMP reaction mixture.
Wipe off any water on the surface of the chip.
Place the droplet counting microwell chip on the microscope counter.
Open the imaging software and select appropriate scan modes.
Adjust the microscope to focus clearly on the droplets through eyepieces.
Setup image acquisition parameters for 488 (FITC), 560 (TAMRA), and 640 (Cy5) channels.
Optimize imaging parameters until positive droplets are brightly fluorescent under observation.
Save optimized parameters for later use.
Use the large image scan function to image all droplets.
Set the scan parameters: pixel size is 2.49 μm, optical resolution is 0.78 μm, scan size is 512 × 512 pixels, and dwell time is 2.2 μs.
Save the scanned large image and image other samples under the same microscopy parameters.
Clean the chips after all sample scans are finished.
Inject isopropanol to clean the chips.
Incubate with 2 U/μL DNase I at 37°C for 8–12 h to degrade residual oligonucleotides.
Analyze the pictures using NIS-Element software (or other image analysis software).
Click the toolbar and choose View > Analysis Controls > Automated Measurement > Thresholding > Per channel.
Define values for fluorescence intensity threshold, droplet size ranges, circularity, and other parameters.
Set the 488 channel threshold above the non-droplet background fluorescence to ensure counting all droplets.
Set the 560/640 channels threshold above the non-fluorescent droplets to count only positive droplets.
Adjust the threshold range to ensure correct counting of droplets.
Convert the droplet diameter (∼50 μm) into image pixels.
Define min/max values for droplet size as 10/60 μm of the mean droplet diameter.
Set the minimum diameter to 10 μm to count droplets around the edge of photographs.
Perform 'Clean' operation on the binary layer to remove small objects from the image if needed.
Smooth the binary image contours using the 'Smooth' operation if required.
Fill holes within binary objects using the 'Fill Holes' operation when necessary.
Separate objects in the binary layer with the 'Separate' operation as appropriate.
Obtain the number of counted droplets from View > Analysis Controls > Automated Measurement Results.
Save and export data for future analysis.
Follow the manufacturer’s protocol of QIAamp MinElute Virus Spin Kit to extract HCV and HIV RNA from plasma samples.
Store extracted/purified RNA samples at −80°C for long-term storage.
Reverse transcribe HCV and HIV RNA into cDNAs according to the instruction of the QuantiTect Reverse Transcription Kit.
Store cDNA standards at −20°C for up to 1 week.
Dissolve cDNA samples in 2 mL ddH2O and divide them into two equal-volume portions.
Subject one portion to qPCR analysis.
Subject another portion to previously described multiplexed dLAMP assay.
Prepare the multiplexed qPCR reaction master mix in a microcentrifuge tube.
Store the qPCR reaction master mix at 4°C for up to 1 week.
Perform PCR in an ABI StepOnePlus qPCR thermal cycler according to the given program.
Determine cDNA concentrations from standard curves plotted using synthetic templates.
Compare results obtained from qPCR and dLAMP to evaluate the performance of the developed dLAMP assay.
